version.note: The recording appears to sing all six strophes; no source consulted states the performing text or the key of the transfer. Utz classifies recordings by transposition from the first edition, but the value for this song and the absolute pitch of the transfer are not established here.

performers.note: The label photograph of the scanned copy names Kammersänger Hans Duhan, baritone of the Vienna State Opera, with Prof. Ferdinand Foll at the piano; the Internet Archive description names the same two performers. Utz reports that Duhan recorded nineteen songs with Foll on 27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928 and the remaining five (Nos. 16, 17, 19, 20, 23) with Lene Orthmann on 11 July 1928, so Orthmann does not play on this side. The Commons file description names only Duhan.

date.note: The Internet Archive description of the disc that carries this side gives the recording date. Utz lists the same three Foll session days (27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928) without assigning songs to days, so the song-by-day assignment rests on the Internet Archive uploader’s labelling. Commons gives only the year 1928.

place.note: No source consulted names the studio or city of the session.

label.value: Gramola Record (The Gramophone Company (Czechoslovakia) Limited), as printed on the scanned copy
label.note: The label photograph of this scanned copy shows a Gramola Record imprint, whereas the photographed first disc carries the His Master’s Voice imprint; the photographed copies of this set carry both imprints. The label gives no date, and nothing here dates the first issue or shows that the audio transfer derives from the photographed copy.

catalogue.note: The label photograph of the scanned copy prints Cat. No. ES 384, and the Commons file name and the Internet Archive description agree.

matrixTakeSides.value: CK 2950, take 2 (run-out “Ck 2950” with II); side No. 5 (label number 0942028); reverse side: Wasserflut (matrix CK 2951-2). Disc 3 of 12 of the set; 30 cm.
matrixTakeSides.note: The label photograph of the scanned copy shows the matrix and take in the run-out; the Internet Archive description and the Commons file name give the same matrix and take. The set was issued as twelve discs, one song to a side (Utz). The photograph is of one copy and does not identify the copy from which the audio was transferred.

credits.note: No transfer engineer is named. The Commons file was uploaded on 11 August 2015 by the user Patachonf and re-uploaded on 10 and 15 February 2022 by the user Mitar; the Internet Archive item was added on 25 April 2019 by the uploader recordplayer78. These are upload facts, not transfer credits.

date.note: No transfer date is identified. Upload dates are not treated as transfer dates.

processing.note: Both hosts hold a FLAC file. The Commons duration (256.00 s) and the Internet Archive FLAC length (255.88 s) agree within 0.15 s, which suggests the same digitisation; which host received it first is not established, and the source disc, stylus, equalisation and noise treatment are undocumented.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: FLAC

composition.value: Both the music and the poem are out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Schubert died in 1828 and the poet Wilhelm Müller in 1827. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about any modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to this recording, attributed to 1928. The Internet Archive item carries a Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which is the uploader’s assertion and is not treated as authority to waive any rights. The publication date of the original disc is not documented; the EU basis here depends on the recording being first published before 1963, which is inferred from its 1928 session. Not established as public domain in the United States.

alternatives.value: PD-EU-audio — European performers’ and producers’ rights claimed expired.
Public Domain Mark 1.0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item, uploader’s assertion.
